title: The Grateful Crane (Tsuru no Ongaeshi)
summary: An old man saves a trapped crane, then a mysterious woman arrives and changes everything.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, during an unusually bitter winter, an old man walked through a cold wood. The skeletal branches overhead rattled like dry bones against a pale, bruised sky. He sought only a handful of fallen timber to warm his meager hearth against the frost. While he walked, a sudden movement caught his tired eye among the drifted snow. It was a magnificent white bird, its pristine feathers hopelessly snared in a hidden hunter's trap. The poor creature could not move because its wing was badly hurt.

Feeling deep pain for the living thing, the man approached with slow and gentle steps. He knelt in the freezing snow and carefully set the trapped animal free from its cruel iron teeth. The freed bird opened its large wings and caught the wintry draft, rising high into the cold sky. It circled above the trees for a long moment before disappearing completely into the gray horizon. Not once did the old man regret the time he had lost nor the labor he had abandoned. He simply shouldered his meager bundle of sticks and returned to his quiet cottage.

Later that same evening, just as the last amber embers faded, a timid knock sounded at their door. A lovely young woman arrived at the small house, shivering and pale from the biting wind. She explained in a soft, musical voice that she had lost her way in the white cold. With eyes wide with exhaustion, she asked for a modest place to stay until the morning light. The kind old man and his faithful wife did not hesitate to welcome the stranger into their warm home.

They shared their meager bowl of rice and offered her the warmest corner by the hearth. The girl proved to be remarkably helpful around the house, performing daily chores with grace and quiet dignity. Within a few short days, her gentle laughter filled the silent rooms, and she soon became like a daughter to them. They marveled at how swiftly this stranger had woven herself into the fabric of their lonely lives. Yet, beneath her radiant smiles, she maintained a mysterious aura that neither of the old people could fully decipher.

One evening, the young woman approached the couple with a serious and purposeful expression. She told them that she wanted to weave a special piece of material to repay their profound kindness. She entered a small back room, closed the heavy wooden door behind her, and asked them never to watch her work. For several days, strange and wonderful sounds echoed from behind the closed door, resembling the steady rhythm of a distant storm. The old couple obeyed her strange request completely, though curiosity gnawed quietly at their aging minds.

When the girl finally emerged on the fourth morning, she looked terribly pale and exhausted from her ordeal. She handed them a piece of material that shone like silver and ice under the morning sun. It shimmered with an ethereal light, as if captured moonlight had been spun into threads of pure glass. The old man took the wondrous material to the town market, where a wealthy buyer paid a vast amount of gold for it. Because of this unexpected sale, the family suddenly had enough food and money to live comfortably for months.

However, as the weeks passed, the couple grew increasingly curious about how the wonderful material was made. Although they had explicitly promised never to look, the old woman succumbed to her temptation one afternoon. She crept softly down the narrow hallway and opened the heavy wooden door just a little bit to peer inside. What she witnessed defied all reason and filled her chest with an overwhelming mixture of shock and sorrow. Inside the room, there was no girl at all, but a thin white bird was plucking its own feathers to weave into the fabric.

The exhausted bird noticed the shadow at the door, turned its head, and realized with a start that its secret was now known. The bird flew clumsily out the open window, its remaining feathers fluttering in the draft, and transformed back into the lovely young woman mid-air. She spoke to them with deep pain in her voice, explaining that she was the very bird which the man had saved in the woods. Because her true identity had been discovered, she could no longer stay with them as a human being. She thanked them sincerely for their past help, spread her magnificent white wings, and flew away forever into the clouds.

The old man and his wife lived on in quiet solitude after the bird left their home forever. They remembered the lovely young woman who had brought such immense wonder into their daily life. Every single morning, the old man would walk near the edge of the wood and look up at the high sky. He hoped against hope that he might catch a glimpse of the white bird flying far away from any danger. Sometimes the old woman would sit quietly by the window and think about the secret room where the magic had occurred.

They never forgot the strange days when the girl made the shining material inside the little house. Even though she was gone, her memory remained alive within their grateful hearts every single day. The couple always reminded each other that deep care and unselfish actions brought a true blessing to their door. Many years passed after the bird departed from the small home, leaving them with only their memories. The old man and his wife often talked about the wonderful days they had shared before the door had opened.

They remembered how the young woman had brought sudden light and purpose into their quiet lives. The house was often silent, but a lingering love remained deep within their aging hearts. They walked together slowly through the overgrown garden whenever the weather was mild and pleasant. The memory of the white bird gave them profound peace as they faced the twilight of their years. Life went on slowly and peacefully for the old couple who had learned the true value of mercy.

Every afternoon without fail, the old man sat outside on the porch and looked toward the distant wood. He wondered if the white bird was safe and warm in the high, endless sky. The old woman prepared simple food in the kitchen and smiled warmly at her beloved husband through the doorway. They knew from their extraordinary experience that genuine kindness always brings a true and lasting reward. Their remarkable story gradually became known by people in the town, whispered with wonder from generation to generation.
